title: Residency Canonicalizer + Isolation Attestation generator for Dedicated tenants
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: customers on Dedicated require auditable proof that their tenant data is served and retained only within approved physical/geographic boundaries and that retention policies are enforced. Existing telemetry is fragmented across node telemetry, orchestration metadata, and manual exports. This ticket creates a lightweight 'Residency Canonicalizer' and an 'Isolation Attestation' generator that produce verifiable, time-bounded artifacts for compliance audits.
goals: Aggregate authoritative residency and retention metadata for every Dedicated tenant across allocator, node agent, and control-plane records into a canonical snapshot

Produce signed attestation artifacts (machine-readable JSON-LD + human-readable PDF) that bundle: tenant id, node ids, region claims, retention policy, TTL, signing key id, and hashes of included telemetry

Expose on-demand and scheduled snapshot/attestation generation via Console and CLI; store canonical artifacts in the evidence bucket with proven immutability (versioning + WORM settings where available)
Integrate signer with HSM/KMS for non-repudiable signatures and publish verification helpers for auditors
Emit structured audit events and telemetry so Platform and OpSec can monitor staleness, generation failures, and downstream delivery success
acceptance_criteria: Canonicalizer regularly produces a snapshot containing residency metadata for 100% of active Dedicated tenants within 5 minutes of trigger
Artifacts are signed by the KMS/HSM key and verifiable using the published verification endpoint
Evidence stored in S3 (or customer-managed bucket for private deployments) with retention flags, and a Console view shows the latest attestation per tenant
On-demand CLI/Console request returns a signed artifact and pushes an audit event; scheduled exports land in evidence-bucket prefix /attestations/{tenant}/{date}
Automated regression tests cover node agent failures, partial telemetry, and signer timeouts with defined fallback semantics
Security review completed and runbook for incident handling published
implementation_notes: Component: residency-canonicalizer service (stateless) that pulls authoritative sources: allocator DB, node-agent heartbeat, control-plane routing table, and tenant retention config service
Component: node-snapshot-agent (lightweight daemon) emits local block device metadata, zone tag, and current KV-cache ownership when requested; agent communicates over mTLS with canonicalizer
Component: attestation-signer service that interfaces with KMS/HSM; returns JWS signatures and creates a signed PDF via templating service for non-technical auditors

Component: evidence-broker uploads artifacts to configured evidence storage, sets object-level immutability flags when supported, and writes an index entry to the evidence ledger (append-only DynamoDB table with signed checkpoints)

Circuit breakers: canonicalizer retries with exponential backoff for node-agent timeouts; if >30% of nodes fail to respond, canonicalizer emits a partial-attestation with a 'degraded' flag and list of missing node ids
Verification: provide /attest/verify endpoint that accepts artifact URL + signature and returns canonical verification status and signed trust chain metadata
Telemetry: kpi.residency.snapshot.latency, kpi.attestation.signed_count, kpi.attestation.failure_reason, and logs exported to Console dashboard
Operational SLOs: 99% of scheduled attestations succeed within 10 minutes; on-demand attestations succeed within 30s under normal conditions
qa_plan: Unit tests for canonicalizer normalization rules (region alias mapping, retention inheritance rules)
Integration tests with mocked node-agent and KMS to validate end-to-end signing
E2E smoke that runs on a staging Dedicated cluster with 5 tenants and validates Console listing and evidence-bucket contents
Fault-injection tests: node-agent delayed response, signer rate limit, evidence-bucket permission denied
Security fuzz tests on PDF generator to ensure no template injection
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated: start with internal tenants only (flag: residency_attestations.internal=true)
Roll to 20 customers on Dedicated in cohort A for two weeks, monitor attestation success and ops tickets
Open beta: enable for all Dedicated customers who opt-in; Surface opt-in and historical attestations in Console
GA: default enabled for new Dedicated clusters; provide migration path for historical telemetry ingestion
migration_plan: Backfill: run canonicalizer against 90 days of retention metadata and generate historical attestations stored under /attestations/backfill/{tenant}/{date}
Map legacy residency labels to canonical regions via mapping table maintained in config repo
Deprecate manual evidence exports and annotate existing S3 prefixes to include the new signed-ledger index
notes: Decision: we will sign JSON-LD as primary machine artifact and generate PDF as a secondary, human-facing wrapper
Trade-off: using HSM for signing adds operational complexity but required for enterprise compliance; will provide a 'soft' signing mode for internal testing that uses standard KMS keys
Open: policy for retention override requests from customers (PM to confirm legal path)
Concern: evidence-broker must support customer-managed buckets for Private deployments; will require additional IAM flows
